title: Research audit: sharp guard for rounded chirp packing and carry aliases (no new kappa)
body:
Mathematical audit / scoped refinement; no new kappa.

The retained Gaussian block packs rounded signed components with eight guard bits. This package verifies that choice and proves the least uniform guard for the stated rounded-data envelope: one bit for every P >= 6. Removing that last bit admits an exact coefficient alias even though integer recomposition and terminal-carry checks pass. The result concerns the inner correlation; it does not close PR371's final-rounding issue or establish an end-to-end speedup.

Only `research/chirp-packed-correlation-audit/` is added. It includes the all-length coefficient/index argument, exact checker, deterministic certificate, source pins, local seed-68 claim with three candidates, and an opt-in registered replay. The mathematical sharpness claim ranges over all positive block dimensions and the stated error envelope; fixed dimensions or actual exponential outputs may admit tighter bounds.

Reproduce with Python 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/chirp-packed-correlation-audit
```

Expected: `PASS_CHIRP_PACKED_CORRELATION`, ten passing test groups, and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.

Checks cover 14,720 packing cases, 680 rational enclosure cases, 13 unsafe-guard witnesses, and six mathematical controls. The package also checks source/receipt drift, missing inputs, occupied outputs, and relocation. The standalone optimized replay passed on Python 3.14.6 and the registered replay passed on Python 3.12.2. Existing finite-identity tests and `make selected-record-check` pass. Full supplier replay, hosted CI, full resampling and proof-assistant verification are not claimed.

Base: `49b3157d1d89adcef16df8be98445451672be5ba`. The three consumed source files have exact Git-blob and SHA256 pins in `SOURCES.json`. Refreshed main: `dd6403f7` (full hash in `VALIDATION.json`); consumed inputs and the selected record are unchanged. The overlap refresh covered 843 open PRs and all current discussion pages. PR684 handles Gaussian domain/windows, PR902 handles the endpoint potential, and PR693 handles the distinct upstream two's-complement extractor. This adds the Gaussian sign-separated packing guard and perturbation-envelope argument; no pending-PR code is imported.

Credit eumemic, icekylinx, Artus Krohn-Grimberghe, Effy Elden, Sagar Thakrar, Alan Grillo, Douglas Colkitt, and the Harvey–van der Hoeven lineage. Prepared for Hanson Sun (@bbMisk) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematics, implementation, verification and writing. Apache-2.0; no independent human review is claimed. The selected frontier and upstream sources are unchanged.
